title: API sample matrix and streaming fallback playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines a compact API sample matrix and step-by-step streaming fallback procedures intended for SDK authors, support engineers, and integrations teams. It focuses on common intermittent streaming failures (partial payloads, stalled streams, duplicated chunks) and outlines reproducible tests, canonical fixes, and an automated validation matrix you can run in CI. Use this as the single-source pattern for client libraries and first-line support.

Scope:
- Applies to: Redwood hosted API / streaming generation endpoints and official SDKs (Python, Node, Go).
- Excludes: embeddings endpoints and non-streaming batch APIs.
- Audience: SDK engineers, DX support, integration partners.

Quick summary of failure classes (observed in field):
1) Stalled stream: connection remains open but no new events arrive for >10s.
2) Partial final message: stream closes before final 'done' event or with truncated JSON.
3) Duplicate/overlapping chunks: tokens repeated across chunk boundaries.
4) Early close with HTTP 2xx: stream terminated cleanly but application-level completion missing.
5) Backpressure/slow consumer: client buffer limits cause reordering or stalls under high concurrency.

Fast triage checklist (first 6 minutes):
1. Reproduce locally with the same SDK version and network path.
2. Capture a raw network trace (curl --http2 --raw or tcpdump/wireshark for internal reproductions).
3. Request the user submit SDK telemetry: request_id, model, seq_length, streaming=true flag, region.
4. Check the runtime router logs for fallback events and model-variant switching within +/− 30s of the request_id.
5. Validate webhook/ingress timeouts and client-side socket timeouts (common mismatch).
6. If the user reports duplicates, extract two adjacent chunks and diff token offsets.

Canonical fixes (ranked):
- Client socket/read timeouts: make SDK default read timeout = 30s, retry policy = exponential backoff (base 200ms, max 3s), max retries = 2 for transient TCP resets.
- Idempotency and finalization: require a final 'stream:done' marker from server; if missing after retries, SDK should treat the stream as "incomplete" and surface a recoverable error with raw buffer attached.
- Chunk deduplication: add a token-offset header or sequence_id per chunk in SDK transport; dedupe on sequence_id collisions and log at DEBUG level.
- Backpressure handling: increase internal read buffer to 512KB by default and expose config. Encourage consumers to read streams asynchronously using provided iterator helpers.
- Fallback routing transparency: when the server falls back to a higher-latency variant due to capacity, include header X-Redwood-Fallback: true with variant-id; SDK should surface this as a non-fatal warning.

API examples and quick samples (minimal, copyable)

1) Curl raw streaming check (HTTP/2)
$ curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --http2 "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-4-streaming&stream=true"

2) Python (async iterator helper pattern)
>>> from redwood import AsyncClient
>>> client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'], read_timeout=30)
>>> async for event in client.stream("redwood-4-streaming", prompt="Hello", max_tokens=100):
...     if event.type == 'token':
...         process_token(event.text)
...     elif event.type == 'done':
...         finish()

Note: AsyncClient automatically deduplicates by sequence_id header and surfaces incomplete streams as IncompleteStreamError with raw_buffer attribute.

3) Node (stream iterator helper + retry)
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/runtime')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, readTimeoutMs: 30000 })
for await (const chunk of client.streamGenerator('redwood-4-streaming', { prompt: 'Hi' })) {
  if (chunk.type === 'token') console.log(chunk.text)
  if (chunk.type === 'done') console.log('complete')
}

End-to-end validation matrix (ASCII table you can paste into CI output):

| Scenario | Positive criteria | Test command / harness | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal stream | All tokens delivered, 'done' event, <200ms p50 chunk latency | curl raw + python async consumer | SDK CI |
| Stalled stream (server delay) | SDK retries according to policy and resumes, no duplicate tokens | Fault injector: delay middle chunks 15s | Runtime team |
| Partial final message | SDK marks IncompleteStreamError and attaches raw_buffer | Close server socket after final partial JSON | Support/SDK |
| Duplicate chunks | Dedupe by sequence_id, final reconstructed text matches golden | Send overlapping chunk sequences | SDK primitives |
| High concurrency backpressure | No reordering, system memory < 70% node | Run concurrency harness (1000 concurrent streams) | Perf team |

Note: implement this matrix in CI using the redwood-stream-harness (see related pages).

Observability and telemetry guidelines
- Required spans: request.send, transport.receive_chunk, chunk.dedup, stream.finalization.
- Minimum logs: warn when stream stalls >10s, debug when sequence_id mismatch detected, info when fallback header is present.
- Suggested metrics (per-route): stream_success_rate, avg_chunk_latency_ms, dedup_ratio, incomplete_stream_rate.
- Traces should include request_id and sample raw_buffer (first 2KB) for incomplete streams only (PII scrubbed).

Rollout checklist for SDK patch that addresses streaming issues
1. Implement helper iterator that normalizes chunk shape across transports (HTTP/1.1 SSE, HTTP/2, WebSocket).
2. Add unit tests for dedupe, timeouts, and incomplete finalization.
3. Add integration harness tests that start a local mock server capable of injecting: delays, truncated frames, duplicate frames, early close.
4. Bump default read timeout to 30s and expose env var REDWOOD_SDK_READ_TIMEOUT.
5. Publish release candidate to internal package feed and attach the streaming-harness output for the release notes.
6. Notify support and update public SDK docs with a short troubleshooting section.

Backwards compatibility notes
- Changing the default read timeout is non-breaking but may surface latent bugs in user code that assumed shorter timeouts. Communicate change in changelog and include migration FAQ.
- Sequence_id header is additive; servers that don’t send it will have SDK fallback to token-offset dedupe with slightly higher false-positive risk.

Support playbook (when escalated to runtime or infra)
1. Provide request_id, raw network capture, SDK version, region, and test harness run id.
2. If streaming failure correlates with router fallback events, engage runtime with timeframe and sample logs (router-<id>.log).
3. If root cause is client environment (proxies, corporate middleboxes), provide the curl --http2 --raw reproduction and recommend WebSocket fallback.
4. For customer-sensitive or regulated data, attach only scrubbed traces and follow the incident evidence SOP.

Samples of canonical error messages the SDK should surface
- IncompleteStreamError: "stream closed before 'done' event; attached raw_buffer"
- StreamStallWarning: "no chunk received in 10s; retrying (1/2)"
- StreamFallbackInfo: "routed to fallback variant (variant-id: r4-fallback-2)"

FAQ
Q: What if my downstream client can't handle async iterators?
A: Provide a sync wrapper that buffers tokens for up to 100ms and yields batch tokens; document memory/latency tradeoffs.

Q: When should we use WebSocket vs HTTP/2 streaming?
A: Use HTTP/2 SSE for simple server-to-client token streams and low-connection overhead. Use WebSocket for bidirectional contexts or when corporate proxies block HTTP/2. Document both in SDK examples.

Ownership and maintenance:
- Owner: eng-developer-experience / SDK team (primary), Runtime infra (secondary).
- Review cadence: quarterly for defaults and after any production fallback incident.
